transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is... well, my shoulders and neck just stay clenched all day long. It's like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. And by the time evening rolls around, my jaw aches so badly that I can hardly even enjoy playing my guitar anymore.
Is the pain in your jaw, shoulders, and neck the main thing that's bothering you?

Well, the physical tension is definitely a big part of it, but... no, it's not just the pain. It's more like my mind is constantly racing, and the physical stuff is just the result of that. I'm just always worried about something.
Are you worried about specific things or is it more of a general feeling of anxiety that's always there?

Well, it's... it's a lot of specific things, but they just never stop. My mind keeps circling from one thing to the next. Like, I'll worry about whether I'll ever get hired again, or... or if I've somehow completely ruined my reputation with the parents. 

Then it jumps to the future, and I start stressing over whether my retirement is just slipping away. It even happens with the really little things. I'll make a small mistake during a story-time activity, and suddenly I'm agonizing over whether that means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. It's just a constant loop of those kinds of thoughts.
Are you often worried about your own health?

No, not really. I mean, aside from the muscle aches and the jaw pain I mentioned, I don't really worry about getting sick or having some kind of disease. My health is actually pretty fine. It's just... yeah, it's mostly the work and the future stuff that I can't stop thinking about.
Would you say that most of your worries tend to revolve around a single area of your life, like work?

Well, work is definitely the biggest one right now, but... no, I wouldn't say it's just a single area. It's more like it starts with work or the parents, and then it just spills over. 

If I'm not worrying about my job, I'm worrying about my finances, or my retirement, or just making a fool of myself in general. It feels like my brain just finds whatever is available to stress about, so it really covers a lot of ground, not just one specific thing.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel sad or... or depressed. It's more just this constant feeling of being on edge or overwhelmed by all the worrying. But I don't feel down in that way, no.
Are your worries affecting your ability to do the things you need to do on a daily basis?

Yes, it really is. I mean, I'm trying to get back into teaching, but the anxiety is just getting in the way of everything. I've missed a couple of application deadlines because I just couldn't bring myself to finish them. And when I do get an interview, I just... I stumble through it because my mind is racing. I even stopped volunteering for story-time at the library unless someone else handles all the planning. It's just too much. So, yeah, it's definitely keeping me from getting back into the classroom in any reliable way.
Do you find it difficult to stop thinking about these worries once they start?

Yes, very difficult. I try to pull myself out of it... I'll tell myself to make a list, or maybe pray, or go out and weed the garden. Just, you know, try to focus on the next practical step. But it doesn't really work. It's like one worry just hands off to another, and before I know it, I've lost half the afternoon to it.
Are there any activities or situations that you've been avoiding because of your worries?

No, not really. I mean, other than stepping back from the planning part of story-time like I mentioned, I don't think I'm actively avoiding anything. I still go out, I run errands, I try to do my normal daily routine... I just worry the entire time I'm doing those things. But I'm not staying home or avoiding specific places or situations, no.
Do you often experience stomach problems, headaches, or other physical complaints when you're worried?

No, not really. I mean, I don't get headaches or stomachaches or anything like that. I know some people get sick to their stomach when they're stressed, but that doesn't really happen to me. It's mostly just... the thoughts racing and feeling tense, but no actual physical pain or stomach issues.
Do you find that your worries tend to focus on a specific type of problem, such as making mistakes or being judged?

Well, it's not really limited to just one specific thing. My mind just keeps circling from one problem to the next. I'll worry about whether I'll ever get hired again, and then that turns into worrying if I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents. Then I start stressing about whether my retirement is just slipping away. And then, yeah, I do worry about making mistakes, too... I'll start thinking that even a small mistake in a story-time activity means I shouldn't be trusted with children anymore. It just never seems to settle on one single issue, it just jumps around all of them.
Do you feel like these worries are unwanted and popping into your mind without you intentionally thinking about them?

Yes, absolutely. I don't want to be thinking about these things at all. I try telling myself to, you know, make a list, or pray, or go out and weed the garden... just try to focus on the next practical step. But it doesn't really work. They just keep popping up. One worry just hands off to another, and before I know it, I've lost half the afternoon just sitting there, completely caught up in it. I can't seem to stop them once they start.
Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your overall well-being?

Yes, it really is. I mean, it's definitely affecting my life right now. Because I get so caught up in it, I've actually missed application deadlines. And when I do manage to get an interview, I just end up stumbling through the whole thing. I've even stopped volunteering for story-time unless someone else handles all the planning for it. So, yeah, the anxiety is basically keeping me from getting back into the classroom in any reliable way.
Would you say that your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?

Yes, it really is. It's... it's very upsetting. Just feeling like I have no control over my own mind, and watching it completely derail my day... it's exhausting. It just wears me down every single day.
Do you experience any specific sensations, like a racing heart or sweating, when you're worrying?

No, not really. I mean, I don't get a racing heart or start sweating or anything like that. I haven't really noticed any physical feelings like you're describing. It's mostly just... well, just the constant thoughts in my head, not really a physical thing for me.
Are you worried that your physical health is somehow failing or deteriorating?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, my health seems fine, as far as I know. I'm not worried about getting sick or my body breaking down or anything like that. It's really just the stress and the constant worrying in my head, not my physical health.
Are your worries ever about your body or health in general?

No, not really. I mean, like I just said, I don't really worry about getting sick or anything. My worries are more about... well, just life stuff. Work, my family, just the day-to-day things that I can't seem to stop thinking about. But no, not my body or my health.
Are your worries ever about your appearance or how your body functions?

No, I don't think so. I'm not really focused on how I look or how my body works. Like I said, it's really just the everyday things—the bills, the kids at school, my family. It's just a constant stream of worrying about those kinds of things, not my appearance.
Are your worries affecting your relationships with friends or family?

No, I wouldn't say they are. I mean, my family knows I'm stressed, and they see me worrying, but it hasn't caused any big fights or pushed anyone away. We still get along fine. I just... I keep a lot of it to myself, or try to, anyway. So, no, it's not really messing up my relationships.
Are there any situations or activities that you're not doing at all because of your worrying?

Yeah, it is. It's actually keeping me from getting back into the classroom in any reliable way. I've just missed application deadlines because I get too caught up in it, and the few times I've actually had interviews, I just stumble right through them. I've even stopped volunteering for story-time... well, unless someone else handles all the planning for it. I just can't bring myself to do it otherwise.
